sentences.text:
Sonu Yadav aged about 23 years, son of Manager Yadav, resident of Babudih, P.O.-Bishunpur,
P.S.-Dhanbad, District-Dhanbad ... ... Appellant Versus The State of Jharkhand ... ... Respondent ---------
CORAM:
HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RONGON MUKHOPADHYAY HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE PRADEEP KUMAR SRIVASTAVA
For the Appellant : Mr. Jitendra Shankar Singh, Advocate For the Resp. State :
Mr. Pankaj Kumar Mishra, A.P.P.
Heard Mr. Jitednra Shankar Singh, learned counsel for the appellant and learned A.P.P. for the State.
2. This application has been preferred by the appellant for grant of bail to him during pendency of this appeal.

3. The appellant has been convicted for the offences under Sections 376, 354A and 354D of IPC and has been sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years along with a fine of Rs.50,000/- for the offences under Section 376 of IPC.

4. It has been alleged that the appellant used to do obscene acts with the informant as a result of which a complaint was made to Mahila P.S. in which the appellant had submitted a bond undertaking not to harass the informant in future.

However, the appellant subsequently committed rape upon the informant and made a videography of the same and by showing it to her started blackmailing her and established physical relationship with her on a regular basis.

sentences.text: 5. Submission has been advanced by learned counsel for the appellant that the date of the occurrence as per the informant is 04.02.2022 but the First Information Report was instituted after 9 months of the occurrence.
Learned counsel while referring to the evidence of the parents and the husband of the informant has submitted that they have given different dates of the occurrence.

It has also been submitted that as per the evidence of the victim, who has been examined as P.W.3, the initial incident of the indecent act committed by the appellant with the informant was in the year,
2019.

Learned counsel submits that the appellant is in custody since 27.07.2022 and the entire facets of the case would indicate that there was a consensual relationship between the appellant and the informant.
Moreover, the purported video, which was used by the appellant to victimize the informant has not been produced by the prosecution.
6. Learned A.P.P. has opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant.

7. On consideration of the evidence of the victim, her parents as well as her husband and inordinate delay in institution of the First Information Report and also the period of custody undergone by the appellant, we are inclined to admit the appellant on bail.

Accordingly, during pendency of this appeal, the appellant is directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.10,000/- (Rs.
Ten Thousand/-) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Additional Sessions Judge-X, Dhanbad in S.T. No.249 of 2023.
8.
I.A. No.14477 of 2025 stands disposed of.

(Rongon Mukhopadhyay, J.) (Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) 22/12/2025 Pappu/-
